theorems.closed_sat_rule_size: Every satisfiable closed n-variable instance has an O(n)-size zero-input Skolem vector: the bits of any satisfying assignment.
theorems.uniform_synthesis: A deterministic polynomial-time synthesizer for valid zero-input Skolem vectors on every closed instance decides SAT in polynomial time by evaluating F(f()).
theorems.generic_validation: SKOLEM_VALID(R,f) is coNP-complete for polynomial-size bounded-fanin Boolean DAGs; reduction from 3CNF UNSAT uses R_G(x,y)=x OR NOT G(y), f(y)=0.

implications: Skolem rule size alone does not reduce closed-SAT hardness.
Universal synthesis is solver-equivalent on closed instances.
A generic deterministic polynomial raw validity checker would imply P=NP.
Polynomial-size independently checkable certificates for every valid generic rule would imply NP=coNP.
